newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng ekes out new record closing high.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng ekes out new record closing high.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index managed to eke out a new closing record high on Monday, aided by a jump in New World Development shares ahead of the release of the company's results this week.
The Hang Seng index closed 30.13 points higher at 12,559.40, beating Friday's record close of 12,529.27. Turnover was HK$6.34 billion compared to HK$7.3 billion on Friday.

"The market has still done reasonably well given the situation in the U.S," said Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "At the end of the day it's New World that is really keeping it there," he said.
Shares in New World Development closed HK$1.00 higher at HK$47.00 after reaching a record high of HK$47.80 during the session. The company is due to release fiscal 1996 results on Thursday.

Analysts said caution ahead of Tuesday's U.S. presidential election had kept some investors sidelined. They said investors were nervous that a Democratic sweep of the Congressional races would prompt weakness on Wall Street.

"Investors will interpret it negatively and generally investors are looking for some correction and they expect some consolidation after the presidential election," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
Hutcheson said it would be hard for the Hang Seng to break "big new highs" from this point.
"Right now we are trading at 14 times this year's earnings which is pretty high in relation to the historic average which would be probably closer to 11, 12 times," he said.
"You have got some results coming out that won't be treated particulary well. China Light was below expectations."

China Light and Power Co reported net profit for the year ended September 30 of HK$4.84 billion compared to HK$5.67 billion. Deutsche Morgan Grenfell had expected net profit of HK$5.0 billion. The stock closed HK$0.30 lower at HK$35.90.
Hong Kong Telecommunications is due to release interim results on Tuesday. The stock closed HK$0.05 higher at HK$13.60.
Great Eagle Holdings rose HK$1.65 to HK$27.00 and Hutchison closed HK$0.75 higher at HK$54.75. Henderson Land shed HK$0.25 to HK$69.75 and Swire Pacific ended down HK$0.50 at HK$67.25.
Shares in Pacific Concord fell HK$0.125 to HK$2.00 following the weak response to the initial public offering of its Concord Land Development Co unit. The IPO was 1.53 times subscribed.
